stamped reject on "Regulars": Its cost is out of proportion: every pinned schema is paid for on every request of every session in exchange for an unmeasured saving of a few ToolSearch round trips, and the card is a counter nobody would mention.

stamped reject on "Casting": A variation on what exists: the model of a subagent type is already settable in its agent definition and in the Agent tool's own parameter, earpiece-widget already hooks agent.spawn, and the card is a per-type cost table beside ledger and usage.

stamped reject on "Yak stack": Its cost is out of proportion: a model call on every prompt for a three-way classification that will often be wrong, to keep a return address that board-widget and the waiting resume and flow widgets already come close to.

stamped reject on "Out of step": A variation on the waiting situation and preflight widgets (project state checked for you), and its own inventor calls it the least surprising: nobody would mention it to a colleague.

stamped reject on "Unsent": Telling a swallowed sentence from ordinary editing with prompt.edit splices is unreliable, and the card puts on screen exactly the words the person chose not to show; a novelty that wears off after one look.
stamped reject on "The jar": A variation on badges-widget and the waiting mirror and wrapped widgets: a phrase counter with a picture, built on a joke that is already everywhere.

stamped reject on "Deja vu": Word-shingle overlap with no model will almost never fire on a real repeat and will misfire on boilerplate prompts, so the best moment barely happens; it is also another reader of saved sessions beside ledger and the waiting insight widget.

stamped reject on "Trail": Not chosen: the strongest runner-up, but a transcript row scrolls and a card row is clickable only in the fullscreen layout (the call answers 'none scrolls' elsewhere), so in the default layout it is a list of your own prompts; Amendments works everywhere at no cost.
